instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Stay for the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the laptop shut. I've decided you're hearing why I haven't booked our anniversary trip before you start fixing the flights.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought that was all you needed help with.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I allowed you to think that. Here's the first correction: I was relieved when the cheap seats sold out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll keep it shut. Is this about the trip, or us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That question is allowed. Us. I hoped a cancellation would say it for me. Stay beside me while I give you the rest; I need to know you can hear it and still stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm giving you the full account of why I was late to the reunion. Stay here and hear it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saved you a seat beside me. Was it traffic?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That explanation isn't approved. I waited outside for half an hour, and I want you to hear why.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm here. But I thought you didn't want to sit with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wanted that seat. I was afraid you were happier while it was empty. Now you may take the one beside me and tell me whether you can stay after hearing that.

cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Drop the Armor
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The shop's locked. I'm ending your cheerful-voice shift now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone has to keep morale up. You're my only employee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm off the clock, and I'm authorizing an honest answer. What did that empty till do to you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the stockroom. Then I practiced smiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The rehearsal is canceled. You may be upset out here with me; I'm not sending you back into the stockroom to get your face ready.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've heard 'I'm managing' three times over dinner. You're allowed to give me a less polished answer about going home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the silence. I leave the television on so it sounds occupied.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm approving a real guest. Ask me over without pretending you've already got company.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cook. I promise I won't be miserable all evening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cooking is optional; that promise is rejected. You may invite me when you're miserable and serve toast. I'd rather have your company than your performance.

cards.title: I Started the Spiral
cards.instruction: Hide how much your own fear or resentment created the emotional crisis while helping everyone calm it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved a calm update to the stallholders: the fair is still on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You panicked about the forecast and told them to cancel their vans.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then my contact list is complete. You're authorized to tell them the arrangements are unchanged.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're not unchanged. Two vans are canceled because of your calls.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Correction approved: a transport hiccup, which I'm arranging replacements for. Leave my weather worries out of the update; they need a way to get here, not another reason to panic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The club money's in the other envelope. I've approved a message telling everyone to stop worrying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You phoned me crying that the treasurer had stolen it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now you're appointed to pass on the calm version: all the money is accounted for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told the whole committee what you said. They think he stole it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I authorize a call to the whole committee. Introduce it as a routine balance update; I'll explain where the envelope was, and you may leave my tears out of the introduction.

cards.title: Not the Real Fear
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on practical details so no one reaches the fear underneath them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The scholarship letter may stay closed until I've approved the tea arrangements. Have we got clean teaspoons?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made your tea. Open it; I want to know if you're leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This cup has sugar. I haven't approved sugar in mine; bring another cup first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take mine. Are you frightened of going, or staying here with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The swap is provisionally approved. Label the cups before we do anything else; I won't have uncertainty over which one has sugar.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I approve discussing my move, report the train time once more.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six twelve. I've checked five times, and your ticket's in your hand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Time confirmed. Now tell me whether this ticket is sufficient for the barrier, or whether I need the booking email.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll walk you through. Are you scared of leaving me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your escort offer is approved, subject to one check: do you need a ticket to get onto the platform? Settle that before we discuss anything else.

cards.title: Let Them Keep Hope
cards.instruction: Hide discouraging information because you believe hope is the only thing keeping someone able to continue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Let's pack your paintings for the last gallery. You've finally picked up a brush again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If the big gallery rejected me too, I'm done. Did they write?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Their letter can wait. This gallery still needs your best three.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Pick them, then. I can't face another envelope.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle the envelopes. You finish the blue one; there's still somewhere for it to go.

beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Keep the seed packets. The allotment letter says we're on the waiting list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've covered our number. If it's another year indoors, I'm giving up gardening.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my sunny room. I'll move the bed; keep the packets.
